column4: The fresh faces of 75:22 are looking toward their Lord; this verse supplies the object and fulfillment of their freshness.
The scowling faces of 75:24 expect a crushing calamity; this verse supplies the apprehension embodied in their expression.
Fire scorches their faces and leaves them grimacing, another direct way punishment becomes visible on the face.
On the Day of Resurrection those who lied about Allah are seen with blackened faces, placing final moral condition on the facial surface.
When the promised punishment is seen close at hand, the disbelievers' faces become distressed; encounter turns inward dread into a visible face.
The people of the left are amid scorching wind and boiling water, joining destructive heat to a wind-and-moisture pair that reverses the section's softening climate.
The blessed are given a pure drink by their Lord, completing the same passage's fresh face, joy, couch, and spring with life-giving watering.
The people whose faces show bliss are given sealed nectar to drink, connecting visible freshness to its garden drink.
Their nectar is mixed with Tasnim, preparing the identification of Tasnim as a spring in 83:28.
Tasnim is a spring from which those brought near drink, adding a water-eye to the couch, drink, and fresh-face cluster of 83:22-25.
Creating heaven and earth did not weary Allah, and the verse concludes that He can give the dead life; divine action joins absence of exhaustion to resurrection.
Creation of heaven and earth touched Allah with no weariness, drawing a sharp boundary between creaturely exhausted labor and the Creator's work.
The Hour comes so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives, directly joining final disclosure to سعي.
A believer's righteous effort will not be denied and is written down, the preservation that allows final satisfaction with one's striving.
On the Day a person remembers what he strove for, making the remembered effort part of the judgment scene.
The one who feared standing before his Lord and restrained desire supplies the action behind the favorable outcome in 79:41.
The garden is the refuge of the person described in 79:40, completing an effort-to-abode sequence parallel to the satisfied face.
إِنَّ سَعْيَكُمْ لَشَتَّىٰ states that human striving diverges, the premise for labor ending in opposed conditions.
The giver who confirms the best is eased toward ease, an outcome of striving that can culminate in satisfaction rather than exhaustion.
The withholding denier is eased toward hardship, the opposed course through which striving culminates in distress.
Allah makes earth a resting spread, sky a canopy, and sends water that brings fruit from earth; the section's sky-ground-water relation is assembled in one verse.
Allah raises the heavens without visible pillars and directs attention to signs, closely echoing the section's gaze toward the raised sky before 13:3 turns to earth.
Allah spreads the earth, places rivers in it, and grows paired fruits, completing 13:2's sky-earth pair with watered fertility.
People are asked whether they have looked at the sky above them and how it was built and adorned, the same observational stance toward the raised sky.
The earth is spread, stabilized, and made to grow beautiful pairs, completing 50:6's sky-to-earth act of looking.
The heaven is built with power, beginning another tightly paired statement of sky and earth.
The earth is spread out and Allah is declared an excellent spreader, completing the cosmic pair with the same ground action as the section.
The oath by the sky and the One who built it begins a sky-earth pair parallel to the section's paired objects of contemplation.
The oath by the earth and the One who spread it completes 91:5's pair and repeats the section's laid-out ground.
Sheba's sign is a good land with gardens on both sides and abundant provision, a concrete picture of fertile, favored ground.
Their turning away brings a flood that replaces the two gardens with bitter fruit and sparse trees, converting good watered ground into punitive provision.
The earth bursts with springs and its water meets the descending water for a decreed flood, showing the water-eye as destructive excess rather than garden refreshment.
A sent wind can leave crops yellow and provoke disbelief, reversing the rain-bearing wind and green earth of the preceding revival scene.
People are asked to consider what they sow, directing the contemplative gaze to cultivated ground before its true grower is named.
The question asks whether people make the crop grow or Allah does, locating fertile softness and food in divine action.
Allah could make the crop dry debris, marking the boundary between nourishing growth and ruined vegetation.
People are asked to consider the water they drink, shifting the same contemplative sequence from soil and crop to watering.
The question asks whether people send water down from rain clouds or Allah does, explicitly tying drink to the sky.
Allah could make the water bitter, defining the boundary between drink that sustains and drink that cannot refresh.
The disbelievers cannot ward fire from their faces or backs, another final scene in which the face directly receives punishment.
Their faces are turned about in the Fire while they regret disobedience, staging the condemned face inside its punishment.
Fire covers the criminals' faces, a direct facial counterpart to dust or darkness covering faces elsewhere.
A person tries to shield himself from the worst punishment with his face, making the face the exposed bearer of torment.
The criminals are dragged on their faces into the Fire, joining bodily abasement to the punished face.
Those bringing evil are cast face-first into the Fire, another bodily realization of the lowered condemned face.
People call on Allah تَضَرُّعًا in the darkness and danger of land and sea, showing voluntary abasement arising from distress rather than punitive food.
The command to call on the Lord تَضَرُّعًا makes the ض ر ع family's abasement a chosen stance of prayer.
Remembering the Lord inwardly with تَضَرُّعًا and fear presents the root's humble sense as sustained devotion.
The threatened judgment contains choking food and painful punishment, another food whose physical quality torments instead of nourishing.
Feeding that relieves hunger states food's ordinary merciful function, the direct boundary illuminated when punitive food neither nourishes nor avails against hunger.
The blessed recline on couches in green garments, another concrete scene of the resting object in a flourishing garden.
The garden companions recline with their spouses on couches in shade, joining the seat to repose and shelter.
The blessed recline on furnishings lined with brocade while garden fruit hangs near, placing repose inside moist abundance.
Raised furnishings in the right-hand garden echo the raised couches of the section and oppose the lowered condition of the other faces.
The righteous look out from couches, repeating the posture of 83:23 after the fate of the sinners has been disclosed.
The garden addressees are promised neither fear nor grief, excluding the sorrow that the section hears as leaving a mark of fatigue.
They and their spouses enter the garden delighted, supplying the joy-filled condition announced in 43:68.
Allah saves the God-conscious so that evil does not touch them and they do not grieve, another final removal of marked sorrow.
The garden people rejoice in what their Lord gives them, providing the joyful condition of those reclining on couches in 52:20.
Gardens and mutual satisfaction between Allah and the faithful make رضى the final relation of an enduring community.
Allah makes earth a cradle and sends water from the sky to bring forth diverse plants, joining spread ground, watering, and fertility.
The earth is made a resting spread, another direct formulation of the ground laid out for creaturely life.
The question whether humanity or heaven is harder to create introduces the construction of the sky whose paired earth and water appear in 79:30-31.
The faithless one's deeds are like ashes violently scattered by wind, joining lost labor to dry residue that cannot be retained.
Deeds are reduced to scattered dust, another concrete image of work arriving at a dry, fruitless outcome.
The believers' distinguishing trace is visible on their faces from prostration, confirming that an inward and bodily stance can leave a readable facial mark.
A fruitful, well-watered garden is struck by a fiery whirlwind and burned when its owner is weak, reversing fertile provision into loss at the moment of need.
A freezing wind destroys the crop of people who wrong themselves, an adverse wind-and-field scene opposite the moist wind that helps life flourish.
